title: Effectiveness of Iterative Verifier-in-the-Loop Generate–Validate–Repair for NL→Config in Multi-Device Emulation
research_question: To what extent does an iterative generate–validate–repair loop using a formal network verifier (Batfish) reduce critical semantic errors in LLM-generated multi-device network configurations when tested in an emulation-grounded closed-loop evaluation?
confirmatory_hypotheses: An iterative generate–validate–repair loop with Batfish will produce a statistically significant reduction in semantic configuration errors compared to a single-pass LLM output (paired, per-intent McNemar test, alpha=0.05).
A single additional repair iteration yields diminishing returns beyond two verifier-guided repair cycles for the majority of intents in the testset (predefined cumulative pass-by-iteration curve).
exploratory_questions: How does pass probability vary with topology size (2 devices, 3–4 devices, 5–8 devices)?
What are representative root causes for verifier–emulator discordant cases?
benchmark_scope: Public NL→config intent corpus derived from referenced public corpora (see evidence_record_ids); intents restricted to multi-device changes (>=2 devices).
Emulation using Mininet-style containerized networks with open-source routing stacks (FRRouting) and VyOS images only (no proprietary vendor images).
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — absolute difference in per-intent semantic-error rate (semantic-error = verifier-detected OR emulation-observed reachability/policy violation) between baseline single-pass LLM output and the iterative generate–validate–repair pipeline, computed by the registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1.
secondary_estimands: Per-intent mean number of repair iterations until Batfish pass (capped at 3).
Iteration-wise cumulative pass probability (Kaplan–Meier-like curve over 0..3 iterations).
sampling_plan: Confirmatory sample: N=200 distinct multi-device intents (each intent is a paired observational unit). Intents stratified into 3 topology clusters: (A) 2 devices: 80 intents; (B) 3–4 devices: 80 intents; (C) 5–8 devices: 40 intents. Reserve 50 intents for exploratory/discovery (not included in primary paired test). Inclusion: publicly available NL→config intents requiring configuration changes on >=2 devices, unique intent text, no duplicate intent hashes. Exclusion: intents that reference proprietary vendor features not reproducible on FRR/VyOS (deterministic automated filter). Random seed for intent selection and stratified assignment: 42. Each confirmatory intent yields a paired outcome: baseline single-pass vs iterative pipeline.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: absolute reduction of 15 percentage points (e.g., baseline semantic-error rate 30% → iterative 15%), two-sided alpha=0.05, power=0.80. Calculation method: approximate paired McNemar power calculation under conservative discordant-pair assumptions; N=200 confirmatory intents chosen to achieve ~0.80 power under these assumptions. Assumptions: baseline semantic-error ~30%; iterative reduces to ~15%; discordant pairs drive McNemar test signal. Sensitivity analyses: recompute power/CIs under observed baseline rates (post hoc) and treat missing iterative results as failures per missingness_plan.
exclusion_rules: Exclude intents that reference proprietary vendor features not reproducible on FRR/VyOS (automated deterministic filter).
Exclude exact-hash duplicates of public corpus entries (detected via SHA-256 exact match) from confirmatory sample.
Exclude intents failing automated parsing/normalization in preprocessing (deterministic rule).
missingness_plan: LLM call timeout = 60s; Batfish verification timeout = 120s; emulation run timeout = 300s per intent. Single LLM-call timeout retried once immediately; second timeout yields deterministic 'call-failure' tag. If iterative pipeline fails to produce a syntactically executable config within the 3-iteration cap or encounters repeated infrastructure fatal errors (Docker container crash, corrupted image), the pair is handled per the analysis_plan failed-call-treatment rules. All failures logged with deterministic error codes and archived with hashes. No human adjudication; technical failures treated as infrastructure events.
analysis_plan: Primary executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1. Primary test: two-sided McNemar test (alpha=0.05) on paired binary semantic-error outcomes (baseline vs guarded per intent). Primary estimand reported as absolute reduction with 95% bootstrap CI. Failed-call treatment (pre-registered): primary analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary' (exclude pairs where both baseline and iterative are missing due to infrastructure fatal error); sensitivity analysis uses 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' (treat missing iterative result as failure). Secondary analyses: logistic regression of pass ~ iteration_count + topology_cluster; iteration-wise cumulative pass curve; subgroup analyses by topology cluster. Exploratory p-values reported with BH-FDR (q<=0.10) and Bonferroni-adjusted summaries for the planned 3 subgroup comparisons.
multiplicity_plan: Primary confirmatory test: single hypothesis, alpha=0.05 (no correction). Preplanned exploratory subgroup comparisons (3 clusters) reported with Benjamini–Hochberg FDR (q<=0.10) and Bonferroni-adjusted p-values for interpretive caution. Post-hoc tests labeled as post-hoc and not used to support confirmatory claims.
contamination_plan: Risk factors: intent/config templates present verbatim in LLM training data; duplicate/near-duplicate intents between pools; cross-contamination via cached prompts or model-context bleed. Detection: deterministic SHA-256 hash comparison of all intent texts vs scraped public dataset hashes; automated n-gram overlap detector flagging >80% token overlap; per-run prompt-context reset and single-turn prompts. Flagging rules: exact-hash matches → exclude from confirmatory N; n-gram overlap >80% → flag for sensitivity analysis (remain in primary sample but reported separately); evidence of context reuse → discard and re-run with fresh context, repeat occurrences deterministically exclude affected intents. Analysis treatment: exact-hash matches excluded from confirmatory N; flagged high-overlap intents reported in predefined sensitivity analyses. All flags, hashing manifests, and justifications archived. Residual uncertainty: undetected paraphrase overlaps and undisclosed private-corpus overlap.
stopping_rule: Execute the full preregistered confirmatory N (200 pairs) plus exploratory reserve (50) unless a sustained infrastructure fatal error (e.g., host-node Docker image corruption) prevents further safe execution; in that case, stop and report affected pairs and follow the missingness_plan/analysis_plan treatment.
planned_outputs: IEEE-format short paper (<=5 pages) including Disclosure Statement
Execution manifest and archived raw model/verifier/emulator outputs (hashed)
Code and container images for transformations and pipeline (public repo)
Dataset splits (confirmatory and exploratory) with hash manifests
